rationale:
Reasoning: Direct AAA PRS models exist (n=6). Must-pass phenotype/endpoint alignment is acceptable across the leading candidates because they target abdominal aortic aneurysm as a clinical disease (no proxy traits like family history). Disease-specific domain guidance for AAA explicitly prefers the disease-focused PRS-CS AAA family over generic global-biobank PRS-CS-auto alternatives when endpoints are similarly exact, and to pick the highest directly reported AUC within that family without letting validation-N alone override it.

Evidence: Among the AAA-focused PRS-CS candidates, PGS003973 reports AUC=0.882 (EVAL EUR 100%, validation n=7,517), exceeding PGS003972 (AUC=0.69, n=7,324). The global-biobank PRS-CS-auto model PGS001784 reports AUC=0.868 with a very large validation sample (n=350,767), but it is a generic cross-biobank score; the AAA section cautions to prefer the AAA PRS-CS family over such global-biobank alternatives when endpoint fidelity is comparable. Other direct models (PGS000753, PGS002054) lack reported AUC/R2 here, and PGS003429 has lower AUC (0.708).

Recommendation: Select PGS003973 as the best direct-match model and rate direct-match quality as HIGH given strong reported discrimination relative to the broader landscape (AUC well above the catalog median and upper quartile) and alignment with the AAA-specific preference rules.

Caveats: Confidence is Moderate (not High) because PGS003973’s reported AUC comes from a comparatively small validation cohort (n~7.5k) and the variants_genomebuild is listed as NR; additionally, very high AUCs can be optimistic depending on study design/case ascertainment, and covariates differ across models. If deployment requires strongest real-world generalizability across settings/biobanks, PGS001784’s much larger validation may warrant human review despite the AAA-specific preference rule.

Direct AAA PRS models exist (n=6) with phenotype alignment to abdominal aortic aneurysm (no clear proxy endpoints among the top candidates), so must-pass gates are met. Among the AAA PRS-CS family here (PGS003972, PGS003973), PGS003973 reports the higher AUC (0.882 vs 0.69) with similar endpoint description, so it is preferred despite small validation N (~7.5k). The global-biobank PRS-CS-auto model (PGS001784) shows high AUC (0.868) with very large validation N, but is a generic cross-biobank score and is deprioritized by the AAA-specific caution when endpoint fidelity is comparable. Other candidates either lack reported AUC (PGS000753, PGS002054) or have materially lower AUC (PGS003429 AUC 0.708). Confidence is moderated by (i) small validation size for the selected model and (ii) incomplete reporting (unknown covariates/build details) that could affect external-transfer reliability.

Within the PRS-CS AAA family, PGS003973 reports the highest AUC (0.882) versus PGS003972 (0.69), with similar endpoint labeling; although both have modest validation sample sizes (~7.5k), the reported discrimination is well above the typical PRS AUC landscape (median ~0.61; upper quartile ~0.675). Alternatives either lack reported AUC (PGS000753, PGS002054), show substantially lower AUC (PGS003429 AUC 0.708), or are a more generic cross-biobank PRS-CS-auto score (PGS001784) that is deprioritized by the AAA-specific cautions despite its large validation N and very high AUC (noting such global-biobank results can be optimistic). Therefore the best direct-match choice is PGS003973 and overall direct-match quality is assessed as high, with moderate confidence due to small validation cohorts and incomplete covariate/metadata in some entries.

Direct matches exist (6 AAA PRSs) and they pass must-pass gates: all are explicitly for abdominal aortic aneurysm with no obvious proxy phenotype (one is labeled prevalent AAA but still endpoint-aligned). Domain-knowledge for AAA is trait-specific and overrides generic ranking: prefer the disease-focused PRS-CS AAA family over a generic PRS-CS-auto/global-biobank alternative when endpoints are equally exact, and among AAA PRS-CS candidates choose the one with the highest directly reported AUC; do not let validation-N alone override a higher-performing disease-focused AAA PRS-CS when the endpoint is the same. Although PGS001784 reports a very high AUC (0.868) with much larger validation (n~350k), it is a cross-biobank PRS-CS-auto from a global-biobank benchmarking paper and is deprioritized by the AAA-specific caution in domain knowledge. Therefore, select PGS003973 as best direct model; overall quality judged HIGH due to strong endpoint match and competitive AUC relative to the broader PRS landscape (above the 75th percentile), but confidence is moderated by the small validation cohort size and lack of detailed covariate/phenotype harmonization metadata in the PRS-CS AAA entries.

Direct AAA models exist (n=6) and multiple pass the must-pass phenotype/endpoint alignment gate (all are for abdominal aortic aneurysm rather than a proxy trait; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still disease-specific). Confidence is Moderate because PGS003973’s reported AUC comes from a relatively small validation sample (~7.5k), covariates/phenotyping details are incomplete for several candidates, and two different PRS-CS scores from the same meta-analysis show materially different AUCs, suggesting sensitivity to evaluation/ascertainment.

Reasoning: Direct-match AAA PRS models exist (n=6). Disease-specific AAA guidance prioritizes the disease-focused PRS-CS AAA family over generic global-biobank PRS-CS-auto when endpoints are equally exact, and within the AAA PRS-CS family to pick the highest reported AUC while not letting validation-N alone override a higher-performing disease-focused score.

Evidence: PGS003973 and PGS003972 are disease-focused AAA PRS-CS scores from a dedicated AAA GWAS/meta-analysis publication; PGS003973 reports the highest AUC among that family (AUC=0.882 vs 0.69) with similar (small) validation sizes (~7.5k). Caveats: Overall quality is SUB_OPTIMAL because the top AAA PRS-CS scores have small validation cohorts and limited reporting detail on covariates/endpoint adjudication in the provided context (e.g., some fields are 'Unknown'/'NR'), which reduces confidence in external-transfer reliability; the very high AUC from a small validation set could be optimistic and warrants careful review of validation design and case/control definition before clinical use.

Direct matches exist (6 AAA models) and several pass must-pass phenotype/endpoint alignment gates (all target abdominal aortic aneurysm; no proxy traits). Domain-knowledge for AAA is trait-specific and prioritizes the disease-focused PRS-CS AAA family over generic/global-biobank PRS-CS-auto alternatives when endpoints are equally exact, and within that family to pick the highest directly reported AUC without letting validation-N alone override it. Although PGS001784 (global biobank PRS-CS-auto) reports AUC 0.868 with a much larger validation sample, the AAA-specific guidance prefers the disease-focused PRS-CS family when endpoints are comparably aligned. Caveat: the AUC for PGS003973 is based on a relatively small validation set (n=7,517) and some metadata (e.g., genome build, full covariates) are marked NR/unknown, so real-world transportability and calibration should be reviewed before clinical use.

Reasoning: Direct PRSs exist (6). Apply must-pass gates first: (i) phenotype alignment/endpoint specificity—PGS004606 and PGS004607 have matching phenotyping_reported ('Age-related macular degeneration') and trait_reported, while PGS002269 is a proxy/biomarker-driven construction (retinal layer thickness focus) and PGS004952 targets 'Early AMD' specifically (subtype mismatch risk if the intended endpoint is overall AMD). PGS001834/PGS002041 use UKB 'Macular degeneration (senile) of retina NOS' which may be broader/administrative and they report no AUC/R2 here, limiting evaluability. Evidence: Among the gate-passing, endpoint-faithful models, PGS004606 reports AUC=0.71 with a very large validation sample (n=163,011, EUR eval), which is above the typical median AUC in the provided landscape (median ~0.61; upper quartile ~0.675). PGS004607 has lower AUC (0.65) in the same validation set and is trained on AFR GWAS but evaluated in EUR, raising ancestry-compatibility concerns for EUR deployment. Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as the best direct-match model due to strongest endpoint fidelity plus strong, plausibly generalizable discrimination supported by large validation N. Caveats: Confidence is Moderate because (a) reported performance is AUC only (no calibration/clinical utility shown here), (b) validation appears EUR-only for the chosen model, limiting non-EUR deployment, and (c) alternative models (PGS001834/PGS002041) have sizable multi-ancestry evaluation but missing performance metrics in this context, so they cannot be fairly compared on discrimination.

Reasoning: Direct-match PRSs exist (n=6). Must-pass phenotype alignment and endpoint specificity gates favor models explicitly trained/validated on clinical age-related macular degeneration (AMD) rather than proxy/administrative phenotypes. Evidence: PGS004606 (PRS-CS; IAMDGC EUR GWAS; phenotype reported/validated as AMD) reports AUC=0.71 with large validation N=163,011 and clear covariate adjustment, supporting robust discrimination and stability. PGS004607 has weaker AUC (0.65) and cross-ancestry mismatch (AFR GWAS, EUR eval), making it less suitable as the primary direct model for typical EUR deployment. PGS004952 reports very high AUC (0.842) but is for *early* AMD classification and has very small validation N=1,780, which domain guidance treats as potentially optimistic and not a reliable tie-break win. PGS001834/PGS002041 are UKB-derived “macular degeneration (senile) NOS” with missing AUC/R2 and likely administrative/less specific phenotyping, failing to outperform a clean AMD endpoint model. PGS002269 has phenotype inconsistencies (OCT retinal layer thickness as reported phenotyping) and no discrimination metrics, indicating proxy/biomarker rather than disease endpoint. Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as the best direct-match model due to strongest combined endpoint fidelity and large-scale validation with acceptable reported AUC. Caveats: Confidence is Moderate because all top candidates are EUR-centric (limited non-EUR generalizability) and AUC is only one aspect of clinical utility; calibration, ancestry-stratified performance, and intended AMD case definition (early vs late/advanced) should be reviewed before deployment.

Reasoning: Direct matches exist (6). Must-pass phenotype alignment favors models whose phenotyping_reported is the clinical AMD endpoint rather than proxy/administrative labels or OCT-derived biomarkers. Evidence: PGS004606 and PGS004607 both phenotype 'Age-related macular degeneration' (good endpoint fidelity) and have large EUR evaluation N=163,011, with reported AUCs 0.71 (PGS004606; EUR-derived GWAS) and 0.65 (PGS004607; AFR-derived GWAS, EUR eval). PGS001834/PGS002041 use UKB 'Macular degeneration (senile) of retina NOS' and report no AUC/R2, reducing interpretability; PGS002269 is tied to retinal layer thickness (proxy biomarker) despite AMD labeling; PGS004952 reports high AUC (0.842) but is for *early* AMD classification with very small validation N=1,780, which is vulnerable to optimistic estimates and does not clearly match general AMD deployment. Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as best direct model because it best satisfies endpoint fidelity and has strong validation support; its AUC (0.71) is above the overall PGS landscape median and near/above the upper-quartile range, with substantially stronger reliability than small-N alternatives. Caveats: Evidence here is primarily EUR-based (DEV GWAS EUR; EVAL EUR), so transfer to non-EUR ancestries may be limited; AUC is cohort- and case-definition-dependent and may not replicate under different clinical ascertainment (e.g., incident vs prevalent, early vs late AMD subtypes).

Reasoning: Prefer direct AMD clinical endpoint models that pass phenotype-alignment and endpoint-specificity gates, then rank by endpoint fidelity, external-transfer reliability, discrimination, and validation N (with validation N favored when performance is close). Evidence: (1) PGS002269 fails/violates phenotype-alignment because phenotyping_reported is retinal layer thickness (a biomarker/proxy) rather than AMD case status, so it is down-ranked despite large validation. (2) PGS001834 and PGS002041 use UKB-derived ‘Macular degeneration (senile) of retina NOS’ with no reported AUC/R2, limiting clinical interpretability and making them hard to rank as high-quality for deployment. (3) Among models with clear AMD disease phenotyping and reported discrimination, PGS004606 (PRS-CS; GWAS EUR/IAMDGC; AUC 0.71) and PGS004952 (52 SNPs; AUC 0.842) both have aligned AMD phenotypes, but PGS004952 is validated in a very small sample (n=1,780) and targets *early* AMD under a specific clinical classification, raising endpoint-mismatch/overfitting and small-N optimism concerns; meanwhile PGS004606 is validated at much larger scale (n=163,011), which domain guidance prioritizes when the endpoint is at least as faithful and performance differences may be unstable due to small validation N. Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as the best direct-match model because it has strong phenotype alignment to AMD, reported discrimination, and substantially stronger validation support, making it more reliable for generalizable use than a higher-AUC score evaluated in a tiny cohort. Caveats: All top candidates here appear primarily EUR-based (GWAS EUR; eval EUR), so portability to non-EUR populations is uncertain; the ‘senile retina NOS’ UKB phenotypes may represent heterogeneous AMD definitions; and the large AUC gap vs PGS004952 could reflect different endpoints (early AMD vs broader AMD) rather than true superiority of either score.

Reasoning: Direct matches exist (6). Apply must-pass phenotype/endpoint alignment: PGS002269 is a proxy/biomarker-driven construction (retinal layer thickness phenotyping reported) rather than a clean AMD clinical endpoint, so it is down-ranked. PGS001834 and PGS002041 use a UKB administrative/broad AMD code label and provide no AUC/R2, limiting clinical interpretability. PGS004952 targets early AMD (clinical classification) with high AUC but has a very small validation sample (n=1,780), so the apparent discrimination is likely optimistic/unstable relative to larger validations. This leaves PGS004606 and PGS004607 as clinically aligned AMD endpoint models with reported AUC and large validation (n=163,011). Evidence: PGS004606 (PRS-CS; GWAS EUR/IAMDGC; EVAL EUR; AUC=0.71; validation n=163,011) has stronger reported discrimination than PGS004607 (AUC=0.65) while maintaining high endpoint fidelity and large validation. Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as best direct-match model because it passes phenotype alignment, has reported performance in a large validation set, and sits above the typical PRS AUC landscape median while avoiding the small-N inflation risk seen in PGS004952. Caveats: Confidence is Moderate because (i) validation appears EUR-only, so portability to non-EUR is uncertain; (ii) AUC depends on case definition and covariate adjustment (age/sex/PCs) and may shift under different clinical ascertainment; (iii) UKB-coded AMD models could be relevant for UKB-like deployments but lack reported AUC/R2 here.

Reasoning: Direct PRS models for age-related macular degeneration (AMD) exist (6 candidates), but the set has important limitations for high-confidence selection given endpoint/validation concerns and missing performance reporting in several candidates. Evidence: Must-pass phenotype alignment/end-point fidelity gate eliminates or down-ranks proxy/ambiguous endpoints: PGS002269 is flagged by phenotyping_reported as retinal layer thickness (a biomarker/proxy), not AMD case status, so it should not be preferred for clinical AMD risk despite large validation N. PGS001834 and PGS002041 use UKB ‘Macular degeneration (senile) of retina NOS’ and report no AUC/R2, limiting comparability; additionally they come from a UKB portability paper where within-ecosystem derivation/validation can complicate external-transfer interpretation. Two 2024 AMD-specific PRS-CS scores (PGS004606, PGS004607) have aligned AMD phenotyping and large validation size (n=163,011) with reported AUC (0.71 and 0.65 respectively). PGS004952 reports a very high AUC (0.842) but is for early AMD specifically and is validated in a very small sample (n=1,780), triggering the domain-knowledge caution that a large AUC edge from tiny validation should not outweigh a more robustly validated model; it is also not clearly matched if the intended endpoint is overall/any AMD. Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as the best direct match because it has strong endpoint alignment (AMD), substantially larger validation sample size, and discrimination above the broader PRS performance landscape median (AUC 0.71 vs ~0.61), while avoiding proxy endpoints and tiny validation-N inflation risk. Caveats: Confidence is not High because (i) several direct models lack AUC/R2, limiting full benchmarking; (ii) PGS004606 appears EUR-derived and EUR-evaluated, so ancestry transfer outside EUR is uncertain; (iii) if the deployment endpoint is specifically early AMD (rather than any/late AMD), PGS004952 could be more phenotype-matched but remains limited by small validation N and should be independently re-validated.

Reasoning: Direct AMD PRS models exist, so selection hinges on must-pass gates (phenotype alignment/specificity) before ranking by validation support and discrimination.

Evidence: Among candidates, PGS004606 and PGS004607 have strongest endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = age-related macular degeneration) and report AUC. PGS001834/PGS002041 use a broader/less specific UKB-style phenotype label (“Macular degeneration (senile) of retina NOS”) and provide no AUC/R2, limiting interpretability despite decent validation N. PGS002269 shows phenotype mismatch (retinal layer thickness biomarker proxy), failing/being heavily down-ranked by phenotype-alignment gate. PGS004952 targets “Early AMD” specifically and, while it reports high AUC (0.842), it is supported by a very small validation sample (n=1,780), so it is less reliable for general AMD deployment than a closely aligned model validated at scale.

Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as the best direct-match model because it aligns to the clinical AMD endpoint, has large validation support (n=163,011; well above the catalog median), and shows discriminative performance (AUC=0.71; above typical median AUC in the landscape). Also, its EUR-trained GWAS base is consistent with its EUR evaluation setting.

Caveats: Confidence is Moderate (not High) because (1) model performance is reported only as AUC without additional calibration/clinical operating-point details here, and (2) PGS004952’s higher AUC cannot be fully adjudicated without assessing its small validation design and the intended target (early AMD vs overall AMD). Ancestry portability beyond EUR for PGS004606 is not established in this context.

Reasoning: Multiple direct-match PRSs exist for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Must-pass phenotype alignment and endpoint-specificity gates favor models where both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly AMD (clinical disease) rather than proxy phenotypes (e.g., retinal layer thickness/OCT biomarker) or broad/administrative labels without clear clinical definition. Evidence: PGS004606 and PGS004607 have phenotype alignment (reported/phenotyped as AMD) and provide discrimination (AUC 0.71 and 0.65, respectively) with very large validation (n=163,011), which is well above the landscape median and supports reliable estimation. PGS004952 reports a much higher AUC (0.842) but is validated in a very small cohort (n=1,780) and targets early AMD classification specifically, making it less reliable as a general AMD clinical endpoint score under the validation sample-size tie-break and endpoint-fidelity considerations. PGS001834/PGS002041 are based on a UKB “macular degeneration (senile) NOS” phenotype and report no AUC/R2 here, limiting evaluability. PGS002269 shows phenotype mismatch (OCT photoreceptor layer thickness proxy) and is down-ranked by the phenotype-alignment gate. Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as the best direct model due to strong endpoint fidelity (AMD), strong validation support (n=163k), and acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.71), consistent with domain guidance prioritizing endpoint fidelity and large validation over potentially optimistic small-N AUC. Caveats: Confidence is Moderate because AMD is phenotypically heterogeneous (early vs late, dry vs neovascular) and the context does not specify intended deployment phenotype/subtype; if the target is specifically early AMD classification, PGS004952 may be more endpoint-matched but remains limited by small validation size. Additionally, ancestry match should be checked for the intended population (PGS004606 is EUR-trained/validated).

Reasoning: Prefer direct disease-endpoint PRS with high phenotype alignment and strong, well-powered validation; de-emphasize proxy phenotypes and be cautious with high AUC from small or potentially non-generalizable validations.

Evidence: Among 6 direct matches, PGS004606 (PRS-CS; IAMDGC EUR GWAS; phenotyping_reported = age-related macular degeneration) has good endpoint fidelity and a large EUR evaluation set (validation n=163,011) with AUC=0.71, which is above the overall catalog AUC median (~0.61) and near/above the upper-quartile band (~0.675). PGS004607 has same evaluation N but lower AUC (0.65) and ancestry mismatch (AFR GWAS, EUR eval). PGS004952 reports much higher AUC (0.842) but is for *early* AMD clinical classification and has a very small validation sample (n=1,780), triggering the sample-size tie-break and optimism concerns. PGS001834/PGS002041 lack reported AUC/R2, limiting clinical ranking, and use a UKB-derived administrative phenotype label (“Macular degeneration (senile) of retina NOS”). PGS002269 has phenotype inconsistencies (validation tied to retinal layer thickness biomarker) despite listing AMD.

Recommendation: Use PGS004606 as the best direct-match PRS for age-related macular degeneration due to strongest combination of endpoint fidelity and large validation support with competitive discrimination.

Caveats: Confidence is moderate because the top candidate’s reported performance is from EUR-only evaluation (limited ancestry generalizability) and several alternatives have missing metrics; additionally, PGS004952’s high AUC could reflect a narrower/“easier” early-AMD endpoint and small-N instability rather than superior general clinical prediction.

Reasoning: Multiple direct-match PRSs exist for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Applying must-pass gates, models with proxy/ambiguous phenotyping or missing performance are down-ranked. The goal is a clinically faithful AMD endpoint with credible validation and sufficient sample size, then consider discrimination.

Evidence: PGS004606 (PRS-CS; IAMDGC EUR GWAS; phenotyping_reported = Age-related macular degeneration) directly matches the clinical disease endpoint and reports AUC=0.71 with a large validation sample (n=163,011; EUR eval). This validation size is above the landscape median and supports more reliable generalization estimates. In contrast, PGS001834/PGS002041 (UKB portability study) have administrative-style phenotyping (“Macular degeneration (senile) of retina NOS”) and do not report AUC/R2 here, limiting interpretability. PGS002269 shows phenotype mismatch signals (phenotyping_reported references retinal layer thickness biomarker), making it closer to an endophenotype/proxy gate concern. PGS004952 reports very high AUC (0.842) but is for “Early AMD” and has a very small validation N (n=1,780), which the domain guidance warns should not outweigh a slightly lower AUC from a far larger, endpoint-faithful validation.

Recommendation: Select PGS004606 as the best direct-match model because it passes phenotype alignment for AMD, has strong endpoint fidelity, and is supported by substantially larger validation, making it the most clinically credible choice among the candidates.

Caveats: Confidence is moderate because (1) PGS004606 is EUR-only in both GWAS and validation (ancestry compatibility limits), and (2) AUC=0.71 is solid but not exceptionally high relative to the broader PRS landscape; deployment performance may vary by AMD subtype definition (early vs late, neovascular vs geographic atrophy) and ascertainment.

Direct PRS models exist for the target space (alcohol dependence/AUD), but none report core discrimination metrics (AUC/R2), limiting assessment versus the broader performance landscape and preventing a HIGH-quality designation. Applying must-pass phenotype alignment: PGS000201/PGS000202 are labeled 'Problematic alcohol use' but are phenotyped as DSM-5 alcohol use disorder criteria count (a clinically adjacent but severity/quantitative proxy rather than a clean case-control AUD diagnosis), so they are acceptable but not ideal for a strict 'alcohol dependence' endpoint. PGS002738 is closer in label ('Alcohol use disorder') but uses a family-history-enriched context ('AUD in individuals with family history of AUD'), which domain guidance flags for penalty due to reduced endpoint specificity/transportability to general-population deployment. PGS002739 targets AFR and is ancestry-mismatched for typical EUR deployment; without knowing the intended ancestry, it cannot be the default best. Between the two most deployment-plausible EUR-validated options (PGS000201 vs PGS002738), endpoint fidelity and transportability favor PGS000201 (DSM-5 criteria-based measure without explicit family-history conditioning) and it has slightly larger validation N (7,599 vs 7,900 is similar; however PGS000201’s phenotype definition is more generally applicable). Therefore: direct match found but overall quality is SUB_OPTIMAL due to missing performance metrics and imperfect endpoint fidelity across candidates.

Direct matches exist (4 PGS). Must-pass phenotype alignment/endpoint-specificity gates: PGS000201/PGS000202 are labeled 'Problematic alcohol use' but their reported phenotype is AUD DSM-5 criteria count (a quantitative symptom-count proxy rather than a clean clinical AUD case-control endpoint), so they are acceptable but down-ranked for endpoint fidelity vs an explicit AUD endpoint. PGS002738 and PGS002739 are labeled 'Alcohol use disorder' (closer to the target 'alcohol dependence'), but PGS002738’s evaluation phenotype is 'AUD in individuals with family history of AUD', triggering the domain-knowledge penalty for family-history–conditioned/ascertained endpoints that may not transport to general clinical/population screening. PGS002739 is ancestry-specific (EVAL: AFR only) and gene-based with 858 variants; without a stated target deployment ancestry and with missing performance metrics, it is less broadly usable as a default pick. Across all candidates, key discrimination metrics (AUC/R2) are missing, preventing a HIGH-quality determination relative to the broader performance landscape. Among the suboptimal options, PGS002738 is the closest nominal endpoint match (AUD), uses a large multi-cohort GWAS (MVP/UKB; n~395,995), and has a reasonably sized validation (n~7,900), so it is the best direct match despite the family-history ascertainment caveat.
